protocol.scope_summary: Queensland Community Pharmacy clinical practice guideline for pharmacist management of acute nausea and vomiting associated with gastroenteritis. Service restricted to patients aged 18 years or over. Covers 'Refer when' triggers (supportive management plus referral), 'Treat (if clinically appropriate) and concurrently refer' triggers (pregnancy, suspected labyrinthitis), key points, patient history, examination and hydration assessment, consideration of possible causes (Appendix 1 differential-diagnosis table with referral actions), development of a management plan (oral rehydration therapy plus an oral medicine per Therapeutic Guidelines), confirmation of management, communication of the plan, general advice, clinical review, and references. Ineligibility for treatment as part of a prescribing service does not preclude a patient from accessing services provided as part of usual pharmacy care.

inclusion.text: Presentation is acute nausea and vomiting within the scope of this guideline, with gastroenteritis as the suspected cause: 'An oral antiemetic may be considered for symptom relief if the nausea and vomiting is suspected to be caused by gastroenteritis, although spontaneous improvement of acute nausea and vomiting is likely (2).'

The cause is identified (or significant underlying diseases excluded) before treatment: 'The assessment approach focuses on identifying the cause (or excluding significant underlying diseases) with a view to expectant management or directing specific treatment.' 'Before starting treatment, identify, treat or remove the cause of the nausea and vomiting (if possible), and ensure adequate hydration (6).'

Management can be delivered as printed: 'Pharmacist management of acute nausea and vomiting associated with gastroenteritis includes: non-pharmacological measures: Oral rehydration therapy to prevent or correct dehydration ... pharmacotherapy: An oral medicine for the treatment of acute nausea and vomiting associated with gastroenteritis mentioned in the Therapeutic Guidelines: Gastrointestinal: Nausea and vomiting (Antiemetic drugs in adults) (2).'

diagnosis_pathways.name: Pharmacist assessment and management of acute nausea and vomiting associated with gastroenteritis (history, examination, cause screening, referral screening, treatment, confirmation, counselling, general advice and review)

steps.description: Obtain sufficient information from the patient to identify the likely cause of the nausea/vomiting and assess the safety and appropriateness of any recommendations and medicines. The patient history should consider: age; pregnancy and lactation status (if applicable); nature, severity and frequency of symptoms; food and/or drink consumed in the last 24 hours; onset and duration of symptoms, including timing in relation to eating/drinking; signs and symptoms of dehydration; risk factors for dehydration or electrolyte abnormality (e.g. kidney transplantation, malnutrition, frailty); ability to adhere to treatment or monitoring for dehydration (e.g. intellectual disability); recent head trauma or injury; similar symptoms in close contacts; exposure to toxins, poisons, bites or stings; recent travel; accompanying symptoms e.g., chest pain or heartburn, headache, dizziness, weight loss, fever, abdominal pain, last bowel motion, diarrhoea, constipation, dysuria, or frequency of urination; precipitating and relieving factors; underlying medical conditions e.g., immunocompromised, diabetes or recent surgery; current and recently ceased treatments (including prescribed medicines, vitamins, herbs, other supplements, and over-the-counter medicines); drug allergies/ adverse drug reactions; medication tried to treat current symptoms; alcohol and drug history. Reminder: Pharmacists can access a range of clinical information in a patient’s My Health Record, including details about current and past medication history, allergies and current medical conditions.

gates.criterion: Sufficient information obtained to identify the likely cause and to assess the safety and appropriateness of any recommendations and medicines
No 'Refer when' trigger present on history (RF-1 to RF-20)

steps.description: Examination: 'Where appropriate, conduct assessment of vital signs.' 'Assess hydration status as per the Therapeutic Guidelines: Gastrointestinal (Acute gastroenteritis - Assessment of acute gastroenteritis) (5).' 'Examine for abdominal tenderness or distention, particularly areas where hernias commonly present (excluding the groin).'

gates.criterion: Hydration status assessed as per Therapeutic Guidelines: Gastrointestinal (Acute gastroenteritis - Assessment of acute gastroenteritis)
No signs of severe dehydration e.g. reduced or no urine output, intense thirst, marked loss of skin turgor, sunken eyes, tachycardia, severe hypotension, increased respiration (RF-19)

steps.description: Consider possible causes of nausea and vomiting: 'A non-exhaustive list of possible causes of acute and chronic nausea and vomiting are presented in Appendix 1. When in doubt of the cause of the nausea and vomiting, the pharmacist should refer the patient to an appropriate healthcare provider.' Appendix 1 rows and their printed actions are transcribed as RF-29 to RF-50 (gastrointestinal disorders, central nervous system disorders, systemic conditions and other causes).

gates.criterion: Cause identified (or significant underlying diseases excluded) and no doubt about the cause
Presentation is not an Appendix 1 condition whose printed action is referral (RF-29 to RF-50)

provenance.section_heading: Consider possible causes of nausea and vomiting

steps.description: Refer when — 'Provide supportive management (hydration) and refer the patient to an appropriate healthcare provider (including emergency services, if required) in the following situations:' prolonged vomiting (>24–48 hours); patient looks very unwell or is very drowsy; significant recent weight loss; abdominal distension or tenderness; rectal bleeding; green, bile or blood (coffee grounds) vomit; fever, neck stiffness, confusion; severe headache, altered or loss of consciousness; isolated vomiting without nausea; history of head injury/trauma; increased blood ketone and glucose levels., including if ketones are 0.6 mmol/L or higher; diabetic or is immunocompromised; recent overseas travel; nausea and vomiting are post-operative, radiation-induced or suspected to be drug or medicine-induced; parenteral administration of an antiemetic is indicated; nausea and vomiting is chronic (symptoms for >4 weeks) (1); the patient has recurring episodes of acute nausea and vomiting; inadequate response to optimal treatment; signs of severe dehydration e.g. reduced or no urine output, intense thirst, marked loss of skin turgor, sunken eyes, tachycardia, severe hypotension, increased respiration; severe pain, or nausea and vomiting occur with chest or back pain. (See EXC-1 to EXC-20, RF-1 to RF-20.)

gates.criterion: None of the 'Refer when' triggers present (EXC-1 to EXC-20 / RF-1 to RF-20)

steps.description: Treat (if clinically appropriate) and concurrently refer — 'Provide initial treatment and concurrently refer to an appropriate healthcare provider in the following situations:' the patient is pregnant; labyrinthitis is suspected (vertigo, nystagmus with symptoms worsened by motion, tinnitus). (See EXC-21, EXC-22 / RF-21, RF-22.)

gates.criterion: Patient is not pregnant (otherwise provide initial treatment and concurrently refer)
Labyrinthitis is not suspected (otherwise provide initial treatment and concurrently refer)

provenance.section_heading: Treat (if clinically appropriate) and concurrently refer

steps.description: Develop management plan: 'Pharmacists must ensure that they are prescribing medicines according to the specified sections of the current online version of the Therapeutic Guidelines.' 'Before starting treatment, identify, treat or remove the cause of the nausea and vomiting (if possible), and ensure adequate hydration (6).' 'Pharmacist management of acute nausea and vomiting associated with gastroenteritis includes: non-pharmacological measures: o Oral rehydration therapy to prevent or correct dehydration, in accordance with the Therapeutic Guidelines: Gastrointestinal (Acute gastroenteritis – Rehydration for acute gastroenteritis in adults) (5). pharmacotherapy: o An oral medicine for the treatment of acute nausea and vomiting associated with gastroenteritis mentioned in the Therapeutic Guidelines: Gastrointestinal: Nausea and vomiting (Antiemetic drugs in adults) (2).' Key point: 'An oral antiemetic may be considered for symptom relief if the nausea and vomiting is suspected to be caused by gastroenteritis, although spontaneous improvement of acute nausea and vomiting is likely (2).' Oral rehydration therapy and the oral antiemetic are the only treatments printed (TX-1, TX-2).

gates.criterion: Cause identified, treated or removed if possible, and adequate hydration ensured before starting treatment
Treatment is an oral medicine (oral rehydration therapy and/or oral antiemetic per Therapeutic Guidelines); parenteral administration of an antiemetic is a referral trigger (RF-15)

steps.description: Confirm management is appropriate: 'Consult the Therapeutic Guidelines, Australian Medicines Handbook and other relevant resources to confirm that management is appropriate, including for: contraindications and precautions; drug interactions; pregnancy and lactation.'

gates.criterion: Management confirmed appropriate for contraindications and precautions, drug interactions, and pregnancy and lactation

steps.description: Communicate agreed management plan: 'Comprehensive advice and counselling (including supporting written information when required) should be provided to the patient regarding: individual product and medicine use; non-pharmacological measures, including the importance of rehydration; how to manage adverse effects; the impact of vomiting on the absorption and effectiveness of other regular medications; when to seek further care and/or treatment, including recognising patient deterioration and dehydration.' 'It is the pharmacist’s responsibility to ensure the suitability and accuracy of any resources and information provided to patients (and/or parents/caregivers) and to ensure compliance with all copyright conditions.' 'The agreed management plan should be shared with members of the patient's multidisciplinary healthcare team, with the patient's consent.'

General advice: 'At the time of initial consultation, patients (and/or parents/caregivers) should be advised to see an appropriate healthcare provider if: the condition does not improve or resolve within 24-48 hours of starting treatment; the patient’s condition worsens, including developing systemic signs and symptoms; the patient develops new, or worsening, signs or symptoms, or signs of severe dehydration; the patient’s symptoms recur after initial resolution; adverse effects of treatment cannot be managed in the pharmacy setting.' (See RF-24 to RF-28.)

gates.criterion: None of the 'see an appropriate healthcare provider if' triggers present (RF-24 to RF-28)

steps.description: Clinical review: 'Clinical review is generally not required. Advise patients (and/or parents/caregivers) to see an appropriate healthcare provider if the condition does not improve or resolve (see Refer when and General advice).'

gates.criterion: Condition improves or resolves (otherwise see 'Refer when' and 'General advice')

treatments.notes: Non-pharmacological measure, transcribed as printed: 'Oral rehydration therapy to prevent or correct dehydration, in accordance with the Therapeutic Guidelines: Gastrointestinal (Acute gastroenteritis – Rehydration for acute gastroenteritis in adults) (5).' Also: 'Before starting treatment, identify, treat or remove the cause of the nausea and vomiting (if possible), and ensure adequate hydration (6).' No product name, strength, dose, frequency, volume or duration is printed in this document (delegated to Therapeutic Guidelines - see OQ-4, HTC-2).

As printed: 'An oral medicine for the treatment of acute nausea and vomiting associated with gastroenteritis mentioned in the Therapeutic Guidelines: Gastrointestinal: Nausea and vomiting (Antiemetic drugs in adults) (2).' Key point: 'An oral antiemetic may be considered for symptom relief if the nausea and vomiting is suspected to be caused by gastroenteritis, although spontaneous improvement of acute nausea and vomiting is likely (2).' No specific agent, strength, dose, frequency or duration is printed in this document (see OQ-4, HTC-1). 'Parenteral administration of an antiemetic is indicated' is a refer-when trigger, not a treatment in this protocol (RF-15).

open_questions.topic: No printed exclusion criteria section - 'Refer when' bullets captured as exclusions
open_questions.observed: The document has no heading titled 'Exclusion criteria'. The twenty bullets under 'Refer when' (page 2) are captured as EXC-1 to EXC-20 because the document directs referral rather than sole pharmacist treatment for those situations.
open_questions.why_unclear: Derivation from a referral heading rather than a printed eligibility exclusion list.

open_questions.topic: Combinatorics of the 'Refer when' list interpreted as any_of
open_questions.observed: Introductory wording is 'in the following situations:' followed by bullets with no explicit AND/OR statement; encoded as criteria_group.any_of (any one bullet triggers referral).
open_questions.why_unclear: Document does not state combinatorics for the bullet list; default interpretation recorded.

open_questions.topic: 'Treat (if clinically appropriate) and concurrently refer' bullets captured as exclusions
open_questions.observed: The two bullets under 'Treat (if clinically appropriate) and concurrently refer' (the patient is pregnant; suspected labyrinthitis) are captured as EXC-21/EXC-22 and RF-21/RF-22, although the document directs initial treatment AND concurrent referral rather than non-treatment.
open_questions.why_unclear: Document does not frame these as exclusions from care; encoded as referral-gating criteria in the same any_of group for consistency with the 'Refer when' list, with the concurrent-treatment wording preserved in PW-1-S5.

open_questions.topic: No named antiemetic medicine, strength, dose, frequency or duration printed
open_questions.observed: Pharmacotherapy is defined only as 'An oral medicine for the treatment of acute nausea and vomiting associated with gastroenteritis mentioned in the Therapeutic Guidelines: Gastrointestinal: Nausea and vomiting (Antiemetic drugs in adults) (2)'. No product names or dosing appear anywhere in the document; oral rehydration therapy is likewise delegated to Therapeutic Guidelines: Gastrointestinal (Acute gastroenteritis – Rehydration for acute gastroenteritis in adults) (5).
open_questions.why_unclear: Dose/strength/frequency/duration are not in this document; no invented values were entered.

open_questions.topic: 'prolonged vomiting (>24–48 hours)' printed as greater-than a range
open_questions.observed: Trigger wording is 'prolonged vomiting (>24–48 hours)'; structured as range 24-48 hours. The document gives a range rather than a single numeric threshold.
open_questions.why_unclear: Ambiguous threshold expression; structured value records the printed range with confidence 'medium'.

open_questions.topic: Gate outcome not stated - confirm management appropriate
open_questions.observed: PW-1-S7 gate 'management confirmed appropriate for contraindications and precautions, drug interactions, and pregnancy and lactation' has no stated failure action; on_fail recorded as 'unclear'.
open_questions.why_unclear: Document instructs confirmation but not the consequence of a failed check.

open_questions.topic: Gate outcome not stated - completeness of history/examination
open_questions.observed: PW-1-S1 and PW-1-S2 include gates ('sufficient information obtained', 'hydration status assessed') whose failure action is not printed; on_fail recorded as 'unclear'.
open_questions.why_unclear: Document lists what to consider/assess but not what to do if it cannot be obtained.

open_questions.topic: Urgency mapping of Appendix 1 action column
open_questions.observed: Appendix 1 prints two action phrasings: 'Immediate referral to an appropriate healthcare provider is required if suspected' (mapped to action REFER_URGENT, severity high) and plain 'Referral to an appropriate healthcare provider is required if suspected' / 'Referral ... if suspected' (mapped to action REFER, severity medium). All 'Refer when' and 'General advice' triggers were coded severity medium because no urgency wording is printed there.
open_questions.why_unclear: Mapping of 'Immediate' to REFER_URGENT/high is an interpretation of the document's own urgency language; no explicit urgency categories are printed.

open_questions.topic: Appendix 1 rows for labyrinthitis and pregnancy not duplicated as separate red flags
open_questions.observed: The Appendix 1 rows 'Labyrinthitis' (page 8) and 'Pregnancy' (page 9) repeat the page 2 'Treat (if clinically appropriate) and concurrently refer' bullets; they are captured once as RF-21/RF-22 (page 2) with their concurrent-treatment wording rather than duplicated with the Appendix action text.
open_questions.why_unclear: Deliberate de-duplication of repeated triggers across two sections of the same document.

open_questions.topic: Appendix 1 table read as three columns (Condition / Presentation and suggestive findings / Action)
open_questions.observed: Pages 7-9 are a single table whose rows were transcribed into trigger_text as 'condition - findings - action'. Rows where the action column wrapped across lines were reassembled from the printed bullet fragments; if a row boundary was misread, the affected entries are RF-29 to RF-50.
open_questions.why_unclear: Table text extraction can misalign rows; findings were kept verbatim and no clinical content was added.

open_questions.topic: 'increased blood ketone and glucose levels., including if ketones are 0.6 mmol/L or higher' printed with punctuation artefact and no glucose threshold
open_questions.observed: The refer-when bullet contains the printed string 'levels.,' and gives a numeric threshold only for ketones (0.6 mmol/L); no blood glucose threshold is printed. The same 0.6 mmol/L ketone threshold is repeated in the Appendix 1 DKA row.
open_questions.why_unclear: Only one of two analytes has a printed threshold; structured form captures ketones only.

open_questions.observed: Referral is always to 'an appropriate healthcare provider' (plus 'emergency services, if required'); the document does not name a service type, timeframe or destination for routine vs immediate referral.
open_questions.why_unclear: No destinations printed, so referral lists record the printed wording only.

open_questions.topic: Notifiable requirement set to false on 'consider notification' wording
open_questions.observed: Appendix 1 gastroenteritis row states 'For suspected food poisoning, consider notification to local public health unit or make a food safety complaint online.' No notifiable-condition, GP-notification or AIR-notification requirement is stated anywhere else in the document.
open_questions.why_unclear: Wording is permissive ('consider') rather than mandatory, so required set to false with the printed condition retained; needs confirmation against Queensland notifiable conditions legislation.

open_questions.observed: No regulation, poisons schedule provision or other legal instrument is cited anywhere in the document; protocol.legal_basis records that nothing is printed.
open_questions.why_unclear: Nothing in the document to attribute to a page.

open_questions.observed: 'Service restricted to patients aged 18 years or over' sets a minimum of 18 years; no maximum age is stated (age_bounds.max_years = null). No weight- or age-based dosing is printed.
open_questions.why_unclear: Document only states a lower bound.

open_questions.topic: Clinical review has no scheduled interval
open_questions.observed: 'Clinical review is generally not required' - no follow-up appointment, reconsultation window or review interval is printed beyond the General advice triggers (24-48 hours without improvement).
open_questions.why_unclear: No interval printed; review_followup records the printed conditions only.

open_questions.observed: TX-1 (oral rehydration therapy) coded first_line=true on 'ensure adequate hydration' before starting treatment; TX-2 (oral antiemetic) coded first_line=false on 'may be considered ... although spontaneous improvement of acute nausea and vomiting is likely'. The document does not use the words 'first line'.
open_questions.why_unclear: Line of therapy inferred from the printed emphasis, not an explicit ranking.

hugh_to_confirm.item: Specific oral antiemetic agent(s), strengths, doses, routes, frequencies, durations and max doses for acute nausea and vomiting associated with gastroenteritis (per Therapeutic Guidelines: Gastrointestinal - Nausea and vomiting, Antiemetic drugs in adults).
hugh_to_confirm.reason: Delegated to the current online version of Therapeutic Guidelines; must be pinned and confirmed before go-live.

hugh_to_confirm.item: Oral rehydration therapy formulation, volume, frequency and duration (per Therapeutic Guidelines: Gastrointestinal - Acute gastroenteritis, Rehydration for acute gastroenteritis in adults).
hugh_to_confirm.reason: Delegated to external guideline; no dosing printed here.

hugh_to_confirm.item: Quantity of medicine to supply - no numeric supply cap or quantity limit is printed anywhere in the document.
hugh_to_confirm.reason: Supply quantity left to pharmacist judgement; local policy must set the cap.

hugh_to_confirm.item: Legal basis / poisons schedule provision under which the Queensland Community Pharmacy prescribing service operates for acute nausea and vomiting.
hugh_to_confirm.reason: Not printed anywhere in the document; jurisdictional basis must be confirmed.

hugh_to_confirm.item: Professional discretion clause - 'When applying the information contained within this clinical practice guideline, pharmacists are advised to exercise professional discretion and judgement...'
hugh_to_confirm.reason: Local policy must define how discretion interacts with automated eligibility/referral checks.

hugh_to_confirm.item: Service restriction 'aged 18 years or over' and handling of patients under 18 (document refers to parents/caregivers in advice but restricts the service to 18+).
hugh_to_confirm.reason: Age eligibility is a hard gate; confirm against current Queensland programme settings and resolve the 18+ restriction versus parent/caregiver wording.

hugh_to_confirm.item: Food poisoning notification - 'consider notification to local public health unit or make a food safety complaint online' (Appendix 1, gastroenteritis row): when notification is mandatory, to which unit, and within what timeframe.
hugh_to_confirm.reason: Worded as 'consider'; Queensland notifiable-conditions requirements are jurisdictional and must be confirmed before go-live.

hugh_to_confirm.item: Diabetic ketoacidosis check pathway - blood glucose and ketone testing (blood or urine) and the 0.6 mmol/L ketone threshold, including what the pharmacist does with the result in-pharmacy.
hugh_to_confirm.reason: Threshold is printed but the in-pharmacy testing/referral workflow and equipment are local policy decisions.

hugh_to_confirm.item: Urgency mapping: 'Immediate referral to an appropriate healthcare provider is required if suspected' mapped to REFER_URGENT/severity high; plain referral wording mapped to REFER/severity medium.
hugh_to_confirm.reason: Mapping is an interpretation of printed wording; confirm the engine's escalation behaviour matches Queensland service expectations.

hugh_to_confirm.item: Pregnancy pathway - initial treatment plus concurrent referral, and which antiemetic (if any) may be used in pregnancy given SOMANZ 'Position statement on the Management of Nausea and Vomiting in Pregnancy and Hyperemesis Gravidarum' is listed only as a resource.
hugh_to_confirm.reason: Document requires concurrent referral but gives no pregnancy treatment rules; must be pinned before go-live.

hugh_to_confirm.item: Referral destinations and timeframes - 'an appropriate healthcare provider' is never specified (service type, same-day vs routine, emergency department vs GP).
hugh_to_confirm.reason: Needed to turn referral triggers into actionable routing rules.

hugh_to_confirm.item: Boundary of scope: chronic nausea and vomiting (symptoms for >4 weeks), recurring episodes, post-operative/radiation-induced/drug-induced nausea and vomiting, and parenteral antiemetic indication are referral triggers - confirm these are excluded from the prescribing module rather than handled by it.
hugh_to_confirm.reason: Defines the hard scope boundary of the eligibility rules; must be confirmed with the Queensland service specification.

hugh_to_confirm.item: Confirm management checks - contraindications and precautions, drug interactions, and pregnancy and lactation (Therapeutic Guidelines, Australian Medicines Handbook).
hugh_to_confirm.reason: Checklists live in external resources; local resistance/interaction data is jurisdiction-specific.
